key_insight: MonarchRT introduces an attention design tailored for few-step, autoregressive video diffusion that drastically reduces the quadratic cost of 3D self-attention while preserving the temporal fidelity needed for high-quality, real-time denoising.
problem_solved: Addresses the computational bottleneck of standard 3D self-attention in Diffusion Transformers for real-time, few-step autoregressive video generation, where prior sparse-attention approximations fail and errors compound across time.
method: Factorized spatio-temporal attention that avoids full 3D quadratic computation by decomposing attention into efficient spatial and temporal components.
Temporal caching / recurrence of key-value summaries across frames and denoising steps to reuse past context and cut per-step cost.
Adaptive, motion-aware sparsity that prioritizes tokens/regions critical for denoising in few-step autoregressive regimes, maintaining robustness where prior sparsity patterns break down.
impact: Enables practical real-time video diffusion by lowering latency and compute for autoregressive, few-step denoising—making interactive and edge-capable generative video systems more feasible for researchers and practitioners.

paper_title: MonarchRT: Efficient Attention for Real-Time Video Generation
paper_authors: Krish Agarwal, Zhuoming Chen, Cheng Luo, Yongqi Chen, Haizhong Zheng
